clue.text: Penniless in London and Cairo away in the distant past

indicators.note: in places the scrambled city's letters between the two letters for the distant past

parts.note: BC, before Christ, stands for the far-off past

indicators.note: away suggests the city's letters gone astray, wandering out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being broke while drifting between London and Cairo long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' scrambles CAIRO into ORACI, which goes 'in' BC. BORACIC (short for boracic lint) is Cockney rhyming slang for skint, meaning broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang heard in London: boracic lint rhymes with skint, so it means having no money.

clue.text: Indicates two mushrooms for lifting

parts.note: the prefix bi- indicates two, as in bicycle
ceps are porcini mushrooms

explanation.surface: A sign pointing out a pair of mushrooms to pick up.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper-arm muscle used to bend the elbow and raise weights.

clue.text: Epic TV series up to formula

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters climb, reading backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: An epic television series rises to a winning formula.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cooking instructions, or any method for producing a result.

clue.text: "I hate to clean", reveals housekeeper

indicators.note: reveals suggests the quoted words are opened up and rearranged to show what lies within

explanation.surface: A confession of hating housework, made by the very person who runs the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'reveals' rearranges I HATE CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the mistress of a large house or castle, keeping its keys.

clue.text: Entrance passage going onto church

indicators.note: going onto says the passage word is placed after the church word

parts.note: an arm of the sea is a narrow passage of water

explanation.surface: A doorway passage leading on to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to delight or bewitch them, as a spell would.

clue.text: Remarkable section of pie diagram reconciled

parts.note: a tall story is a remarkable, hard-to-believe one, so tall can mean remarkable

indicators.note: section of says only a short stretch spanning the two words is kept, the rest of them dropped

explanation.surface: An unusual slice of a pie chart finally makes the accounts add up.
explanation.walkthrough: TALL as in a tall tale; 'section of' takes IED from pIE Diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that are reconciled agree with each other, matching up item for item.

clue.text: Emit pleas about type of photography

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone issuing pleas about a particular style of photography.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique where frames are taken at intervals and replayed quickly to speed up slow change.

clue.text: It can be played in early retirement

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something one could take up after stopping work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' tempts a reversal, but the letters run forward across earLY REtirement.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harp of ancient Greece, an instrument that is plucked.

clue.text: I am shortly to be taking part in a council election — what an idiot!

parts.note: I'm is the short form of I am

indicators.note: taking part in means only a part spanning the two words is used, the rest discarded

explanation.surface: Someone groans about standing in a local council election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking part in' takes CILE from counCIL Election; 'to' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dimwit, a stupid person, used as an insult.

clue.text: Not like night now routinely

parts.note: daytime is the opposite of night
today means at the present time, now

explanation.surface: Daytime routine described in contrast to night.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary everyday life, things done as a regular routine.

clue.text: Clown reported to drink at bedtime

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown

explanation.surface: A clown is said to have a nightcap before turning in.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a well-known British circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot milky chocolate drink is a classic nightcap taken before sleep.

clue.text: Liam Brady played like this

indicators.note: played suggests the footballer's name being worked over, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A pundit's verdict on how an Irish footballer performed.
explanation.walkthrough: Liam Brady is a former Arsenal and Ireland midfielder; the anagram of his name describes how he played.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the footballer's style: he played in a splendid, praiseworthy way.

clue.text: Bombard factory crusher

parts.note: to pepper someone is to bombard them, e.g. with shot or questions
a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill

explanation.surface: An instruction to shell a works that crushes things.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen grinder that crushes peppercorns into flakes for seasoning.

clue.text: Recall being in the chorus

indicators.note: being in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone remembers singing among the backing voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' finds the letters across thE CHOrus.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something can mean to evoke or repeat it, as a design harks back to an earlier style.

clue.text: Girl losing her head about allowance a nonsense

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word wraps around what follows
losing her head drops the first letter of the word girl

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A girl frantic over her pocket money, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing her head' takes G from GIRL, leaving IRL, which goes 'about' RATION and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical, unreasonable, contrary to sense, as nonsense is.

clue.text: Respiratory problem a normal one — all going back to drink

parts.note: SARS is severe acute respiratory syndrome
par is the normal or standard level
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: going back means the word all is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An odd chain of ailments and normality leading to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns ALL into LLA, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft drink flavoured with the root of a tropical plant, once popular as a tonic.

clue.text: Stains die out, when clinically cleaned

indicators.note: out suggests the letters going out of their places and reforming

explanation.surface: Marks fade away after a hospital-style scrubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinfected and made hygienic, as a hospital surface is.

clue.text: Plant having soft joint problem

parts.note: p, piano, means soft in music
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A plant that suffers from a soft back problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called leadwort, a flowering shrub with pale blue blossoms.

clue.text: Be seen at dance — not here!

indicators.note: dance suggests the letters jigging about into new positions

explanation.surface: A demand to show up at a dance, followed by the complaint that someone has not.
explanation.definitionFit: A person missing from where they should be, as at a roll call.

clue.text: Half-mile restriction on one who makes rain said to be for tree

indicators.note: Half here takes the closing two letters of the four in the word mile

parts.note: a ban is a restriction

indicators.note: said to be means the word is taken as heard spoken

parts.note: a cloud seeder makes rain by seeding clouds

explanation.surface: A tangled piece about rainmakers and mileage limits leading to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'one who makes rain' is a cloud seeder; 'said to be' makes SEEDER sound like CEDAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall conifer native to the Middle East, the emblem on the Lebanese flag.

clue.text: Arbitrator of impure fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A judge of tainted style.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee or judge who settles disputes in a game.

clue.text: Swindle has outside chance to run

parts.note: to flee is to run away

indicators.note: outside takes the outer letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A con artist has a slim chance to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside chance' looks like the phrase for a long shot, but here it means the word's end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money, like shearing a sheep.

clue.text: Good bearing from new mine

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the word take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A sound direction, or good posture, coming out of a newly opened pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's look or manner, the air they carry themselves with.

clue.text: Return to London hospital is indicative of bad relative to a squint

indicators.note: Return says the hospital's name is read from back to front

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's Hospital in London
mal is French for bad, used in English as a prefix

explanation.surface: A trip back to a London hospital signals poor eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns BARTS into STRAB. Strabismus is the medical name for a squint.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabismus is the medical term for misaligned eyes, so this adjective describes that condition.

clue.text: Loved one to roam free around the university

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the university letter
free suggests letters set loose to rearrange

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A sweetheart free to wander around campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover or love affair, from the French word for love.

clue.text: Rushed to spend without limitless money

indicators.note: without means a letter is taken out of the word spend
limitless strips the word money of its outer letters down to its core

explanation.surface: A shopper hurries to splash out despite having no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitless money' gives the central letter N, taken from SPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Went quickly, hurried along at speed.

clue.text: Opposed to previous duck course

parts.note: anti means opposed to
past means previous
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like 0

explanation.surface: Someone against the old duck dish on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cold meats and pickles, the first course of a meal.

clue.text: One is in nave, wide-eyed

indicators.note: is in places the numeral inside the church word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone standing in a church's nave, gazing around in wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being innocent and inexperienced, gazing at the world with wonder.

clue.text: Composer gripped by overdose worked too hard

indicators.note: gripped by means the composer is held inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer in the grip of an overdose, having pushed himself too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Overexerting oneself, going beyond the right amount of effort.

clue.text: Provide reassurance about rumoured vacation

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: rumoured means a word as heard rather than as written

parts.note: leave is time off, a vacation

explanation.surface: Someone reassures colleagues about gossip over holiday time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumoured' turns LEAVE into LIEVE, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone's worry or distress, comforting them.
